- The issue is that the Sphinx linkcheck builder (Sphinx version 1.7.6) does not verify local (internal) links.
- The bug report provides a sample index.rst file with one valid external link and one broken local link.
- The expected behavior is for the linkcheck to also check if local links point to existing files.

- The linkcheck builder is implemented in sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py.
- The function to modify is check_link(uri, lineno) within the CheckExternalLinksBuilder class.

- Our patch introduced checks for local links: it determines the document directory using self.env.doc2path and then constructs a file path from the given local URI.
- The patch emits a warning if the computed local file path does not exist.

### 3. Facts still to look up
- How Sphinx exactly handles local links in its documentation building process.
- Any potential side effects or required integration points within the Sphinx project when verifying internal links.

- The provided reproduction instructions and expected behavior are based on Sphinx v1.7.6.

- The patch should alter the check_link() method so that if the URI does not start with "http://" or "https://", it should be treated as a local link.

The fix is to set the maxlength attribute on the widget using the field’s max_length value if it isn’t already set.

• In the __init__ method of AuthenticationForm, add code to set:
    self.fields[self.username_field].widget.attrs['maxlength'] = self.fields[self.username_field].max_length
